_spec.law: Facts resolve to the original verified claim record. A layout rebuild does not reverify reporting.

dek.text: ERCOT warns that rapid changes in AI training loads could fatigue generators. Its proposed limit on power swings was still a draft, distinct from reliability requirements already in force.

introduction.text: A data center can affect the grid through the speed of its changing demand, not just its maximum draw. ERCOT's [board presentation](c27) warns that fluctuations associated with AI training can disturb generator shafts and potentially cause fatigue or damage.

The presentation identifies a risk, not a named Texas generator already damaged by a named data center. It supplies neither company's identity. Its proposed response was a draft operating-guide revision, not an adopted rule.

sections.heading: Different risks have different rule statuses

paragraphs.text: Ride-through requirements address equipment disconnecting during normal grid events. ERCOT described those requirements as already effective. The oscillation limit, by contrast, had not yet been filed and carried only a planned submission window.

The grid operator also identified inaccurate models as an obstacle to studying large-load impacts. It described work with Texas A&M and a separate model-quality revision headed for board consideration.

sections.heading: Models must describe the actual facility

paragraphs.text: The [model-quality proposal](c40) calls for compatible data formats and quality tests. It also requires updated models before initial energization, documenting differences from earlier studies and attesting that the data reflect actual field settings.

A technical committee recommendation is part of that proposal's history. The revision record still marked it pending board consideration when checked. A recommendation should not be reported as the board's final approval.

sections.heading: The next decision is still ahead

paragraphs.text: The draft would limit power variation to {{number:c29}} megawatts per {{number:c29:1}} seconds. The presentation asked the board for no action. Filing the proposal and recording subsequent approvals would establish its operative terms. Until then, the planned limit is not an enforceable rule.
